why:
the error every fallible call in the Rust user API returns. Issue 0783 found `TransportError`, its most common payload, unexported; both are exported from the `nros` facade now, so a caller can match the contents.

phase-427 W10 (2026-09-08) — it now implements `core::fmt::Display` and `core::error::Error` (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/types.rs`). RFC-0089 says the port's error difference (`InitError`/`NodeError` where upstream has one `RclrsError`) is "invisible under `?` and loud under a `match`"; that was half true, because `?` into a `Box<dyn Error>` needs `Error`, `Error` needs `Display`, and this enum had neither. A ported rclrs `main` therefore could not keep ONE error type — it had to `map_err` at every call, which is the opposite of invisible. With the impls it costs one line, the signature, and that is what `packages/testing/nros-tests/tests/rclrs_talker_port.rs` counts it as. `Transport` renders its payload with `TransportError`'s own `Display`, which lives in nros-rmw, the crate that defines the variants (issue 0783, closed by phase-482 W7).
